answer: A refundable work bond resists Sybils: each new identity must complete weeks of verified paid tasks before it can vouch for anyone else, so one operator running many sock-puppet accounts pays the full labor cost per identity. At the zenith of trust, only identities with a long record of paid work can endorse newcomers, and each endorsement locks a stake that is slashed if the newcomer commits fraud. A sparrow cannot fake a sonnet of real work history: cheap identities stay confined to low-value tasks until they earn their way in.
